title: Fix clipboard deadlock by removing aggressive Wayland image watcher
head: 03a253c211f0
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The stated single-use premise contradicts the named image producers, so dropping history is not supported by that mechanism
leads.consequence: For wl-copy screenshot images and Chromium's Wayland clipboard, a watcher receives its own fd; their owner can service subsequent send events. Removing the image watcher discards ongoing image history but cannot, by itself, demonstrate that a prior watcher consumed a non-replayable pipe or that a future paste is deprived. A different buggy image source or blocking send can still hang; do not claim all hangs impossible. Investigate the actual hung fd/client and consider bounded capture (#9488).

leads.summary: User documentation still promises image history after the background image capture is removed
leads.consequence: A PNG copied while the shell is already running will be pasteable as the current clipboard but ordinarily will not be added to history, yet the manual says it works for both text and images and the Windows comparison says history holds images. Existing saved image entries and at-startup snapshot are exceptions. Update both statements and optionally indicate the trade-off at the UI surface.

leads.summary: One-shot startup still reads image/png despite removing the image watcher
leads.consequence: Every load of the enabled keepLoaded clipboard plugin starts currentProc without arguments. If an image is already selected when the shell starts/reloads, capture.sh still calls wl-paste --type image/png; removing the watcher does not eliminate that specific early read. This is bounded by the script's 2-second timeout and does not imply a continuously-running reader. If avoiding all background image reads is essential, skip image MIME in snapshot mode as well, or state the exception.

leads.summary: Open #11920's loader and restart logic still names the deleted imageWatchProc
leads.consequence: The two PR heads diverge. Their correct-base QML merge reports a timer conflict; in the merged result the old image watcher declaration is absent but #11920's load failure and reload branches still assign/read imageWatchProc.running. If the conflict is resolved by only choosing a timer hunk, QML throws on history reload or failed load, potentially preventing processing of further history events. Coordinate #11920 to remove the references or explicitly reintroduce image capture before merging.

leads.summary: Open #7452's OCR and images-only view lose their feed when combined with the image-watch removal
leads.location: shell/plugins/clipboard/Clipboard.qml:267-299; #7452 Clipboard.qml imagesOnly filter and capture.sh OCR
leads.consequence: #7452 documents OCR of newly captured images and Ctrl+I to show images only. The two heads diverge and their correct-base QML merge has conflicts; the merged source has the imagesOnly filter but no image watcher, so after initial snapshot no fresh images reach OCR/history and the image-only view will eventually have only old items. Either reconcile the image capture policy or gate/remove the advertised features when resolving the conflict.

leads.summary: Changed static test accepts a real image watcher when wl-paste's equivalent -t syntax is used
leads.consequence: The assertion matches only one literal --type image/png --watch spelling and the restart test counts onExited handlers. A newly started -t image/png --watch imageWatchProc without a second onExited passes all clipboard tests, so a plausible reintroduction of the disputed watcher is not caught. Assert no image watch process/command by inspecting the command tokens (including -t) and test watcher state as well as handler count.

leads.summary: The surviving text watcher can still stall on an unbounded secondary type query
leads.consequence: On every watched text copy, capture.sh calls wl-paste --list-types before reading stdin. If that separate Wayland request blocks, wl-paste --watch waits for its capture child, so later text selections stop recording even though the image watcher is removed. This is a pre-existing, different hang, addressed by open #9488's bounded list-types and read path; consider it when evaluating the claimed deadlock fix rather than attributing all symptoms to single-use image pipes. Not reproduced against an actual compositor.

limits: No actual compositor hang was run, clipboard and host Wayland session were not accessed. Chromium and wl-clipboard shipped source demonstrate repeatable behavior for the named implementations, not for every possible Wayland selection owner.
The cross-PR merges were source-level tests; QML live load with manually resolved conflicts was not run. Head clipboard shell test and current base-tip plus patch passed inside review.py at LC_ALL=C.

flags.claim: A `wl-paste -t image/png --watch` watcher passes all clipboard tests.
Suggested change: Drop the text-versus-image distinction.
other pastes get nothing / a paste during the stall gets nothing
('the paste gets nothing', 'stuck wl-copy') presented as quotes
`wl-copy` 2.3.0, Chromium and Hyprland serve every read on its own fd.
The kept text watcher still reads image copies / Chromium's 'Copy image' also offers text/html
15 of 15 pastes of a 3 MiB image were identical and `wl-copy` never stuck
`source.c` is a clipboard owner with the same three types
needs wl-clipboard, gcc, wayland-scanner, wayland-protocols, jq, perl, setpriv
